edge_explainer: The shelf's three headline attractions are all wrong or overstated, and the correction is the finding. (1) Share count: the IBKR ACSO.TEN line is a COMPLETED issuer self-tender, not a takeover - 4,833,333 shares bought at a fixed 300p (~14.5m GBP), completing 18-Mar-2026, leaving 33,282,874 shares. The shelf used 36,880,399, overstating market cap 11%. (2) 'Below book' is a pure goodwill artifact: net assets $196.1m against intangibles $163.4m of which GOODWILL $139.4m, so tangible book is ~$33m pre-tender and ~$7m after the tender and Dexibit - P/TBV is not below 1, it is effectively unmeasurable. This is the CAPD-class error. (3) 'Net cash 19% of cap' is a 31-Dec-2025 figure taken before the 14.5m GBP tender and the $7.1m Dexibit cash acquisition; today it is ~6%. Corrected EV/EBIT is ~9.0x trailing and ~11.0x on FY26E, not 8.5x. Separately, Mode B found what the shelf could not see: the +22% single-session gap on 5-Jun-2026 (632k shares, ~10x volume) was Constellation Software Inc. disclosing a 3.1628% stake - so ~22% of today's price is unconfirmed-bid speculation, and Constellation itself bought at ~260p, 15% below the market. Ruling is DERAILMENT not de-rate: FY26 guidance is revenue -5.9% and Cash EBITDA -13.1% because two major customers on the SAME core software solution were lost or repriced down (RNS 5-Jan and 29-Jan-2026). NOTE THE HONESTY BOUNDARY: accesso's own disclosure is CLEAN - it capitalises only 6.7% of development spend (unusually conservative for software), defines Cash EBITDA net of capitalised development, pre-announced the customer losses early, and disclosed the 3-Aug IT security incident promptly. The divergence is between the SCREEN's takeaway and the data, not between management's takeaway and the data. Log as a data-quality catch, NOT a management-integrity catch.
